claims.statement: The local smoke verifies exact Signal Siege v1/v2 discovery, durable solo completion and recovery, the complete social, player-report, and MFA slice, and a real two-authority QML challenge, alternating versus match, terminal result, refetch, and minimal synchronization evidence.

Smoke mode runs the QML connector offscreen; the shell exits after the exact health handshake while dedicated live QML scenarios exercise account, MFA, social and report, and two-authority game flows against the migrated server.

The canonical diff gate runs 21 stages covering production static and documentation checks, cartridge contract, renderer, SDK and isolated proof, native client source admission and extracted-package smoke, sequential PostgreSQL tests, the live Rust/API/QML first-playable smoke, provider conformance, the Door Legends authority pilot, and the isolated platform recovery drill before writing a worktree receipt.
A successful non-fast gate writes a receipt derived from the gated worktree, and later gated edits invalidate that delivery evidence.
Forty-seven database-backed server tests are ignored in the ordinary unit loop and run sequentially against SQLx-managed migrated PostgreSQL databases in non-fast gates.

Persona integration tests use multiple accounts to prove exact public response fields, owner-only inventory and mutation, indistinguishable foreign and absent objects, canonical conflicts, validation preservation, and authentication precedence.

The development stack launches the omarchy-gaming-system-server package with OGS bind and log namespaces, binds readiness to that live child and its listening log, asserts the service health identity, and requires new smoke tokens to use ogs1_.
When no MFA key is supplied, the development script creates and reuses a mode-0600 ignored key file under .dev before starting the server.

Pipeline setup verifies reviewed SHA-512 values for the exact CodeGraph wrapper and platform tarballs before script-disabled installation, and separately builds OpenWiki from its reviewed commit and frozen integrity-pinned pnpm dependency graph.

Pipeline readiness rejects an unexpected CodeGraph package set, tree digest, executable link, or provenance field and rejects OpenWiki version, lock, patch, dependency, or build drift before either MCP integration runs.

Five migrated connection tests prove request direction and privacy, race-safe pending-inventory caps, participant-only acceptance and removal, atomic private blocking under races, and serialization of opposite requests and concurrent acceptance.

Five migrated inbox tests prove transition-only conversation creation, typed body-only messages, monotonic unread state, conversation-local sequences, bounded private durable history, lifecycle send denial, and concurrent send/read ordering.

The sync test module combines focused quota and continuity unit tests with six PostgreSQL cases covering mutation mapping, retention/reset, commit-only hints, real WebSocket authorization and decoder limits, principal admission fairness, and no-touch session lifecycle.

The game foundation test slice proves stable catalog ordering, body bounds, exact-version creation and commands, semantic replay, collision and revision failures, rollback silence, participant privacy, atomic sync effects, and one-winner concurrency.

The cartridge proof creates ephemeral signing keys and a temporary signed fixture, starts loopback-only broker and provider processes, asserts that persona, device-token, and database material are not disclosed, renders trusted QML offscreen, records 120-frame timing and RSS evidence, and cleans up exact child processes and temporary files.

The cartridge proof creates ephemeral signing keys and a temporary signed fixture, starts loopback-only broker and provider processes, asserts that persona, device-token, and database material are not disclosed, renders trusted QML offscreen, records 120-frame timing and RSS evidence, and cleans up exact child processes and temporary files.

The focused production cartridge script runs twenty hostile conformance tests, proves deterministic packing across source metadata changes, conforms without network, database, or credential access, installs the exact archive read-only, and denies resolution after revocation.

The focused trusted-renderer script runs two renderer unit tests and nine integration tests, generates real signed Core and Rich-2D packages, prepares plans through the production CLI, and exercises fixed QML states, accessibility, performance, and raster admission under unusable database, credential, and proxy settings.

The renderer harness uses offscreen software rendering and one-CPU affinity when available, measures 120 frames after 60 warm-up frames, enforces frame and RSS caps, validates keyboard and accessibility behavior, renders the largest accepted 2,048-pixel Rich-2D raster, and rejects a 4,096-pixel raster before any plan is published.

Gate 13 exports and verifies the deterministic SDK, builds one first-party repository twice from clean Git clones using copied public tools only, verifies byte-identical signed releases, applies signed lifecycle policy, imports through the secure store, and previews the imported cartridge without database, provider, or platform credentials.

Gate 13 exports and verifies the deterministic SDK, builds one first-party repository twice from clean Git clones using copied public tools only, verifies byte-identical signed releases, applies signed lifecycle policy, imports through the secure store, and previews the imported cartridge without database, provider, or platform credentials.

Seven migrated challenge tests plus one pre-database body-limit test cover private creation and reads, exact replay and collisions, typed inbox and minimal sync payloads, production Signal Siege v2 alternation and completion, exact-session acceptance, terminal history, expiry, limits, rollback, and one-winner races.

Signal Siege validation includes ten deterministic v1/v2 rule tests, one local exact production-catalog and body-limit test, four solo PostgreSQL cases, and the migrated two-person challenge-to-terminal-session case.

The smoke treats its local HTTP responder as untrusted by requiring the spawned server process and listening log to remain valid and by accepting only bounded integer game values before shell arithmetic.

Gate 19 runs provider unit and public protocol tests plus ignored CLI, PostgreSQL registry, separate-process TLS, replay, race, quota, lifecycle, and audit conformance sequentially against migrated PostgreSQL.

The keyboard-first QML fixture corpus runs 41 Qt cases covering production-root accessibility, report submission, social and inbox behavior, contrast, semantics, deterministic and deferred focus, reversible traversal, persistent exit, 640-pixel containment, Escape authority, hostile envelopes, exact retry identity, revision refetch, and active-seat enforcement.

The live game QML scenario creates two independent authenticated authority controllers, challenges and accepts through production REST routes, alternates legal commands until completion, and proves a fresh controller recovers the exact terminal revision and state.

The focused QML entrypoint first enforces a 33-file visual policy that centralizes six-digit colors in OgsTheme, requires every visual Text block to select Text.PlainText, rejects rich or automatic text formats, and checks the required theme contract.

The native client source checker admits only a newline-terminated sorted unique manifest that exactly matches non-test production QML, rejects unsafe paths and symlink or non-regular inputs, binds the package version to the workspace, and validates the launcher and desktop entry before build work.

The native client builder validates source first, computes source and revision provenance, serializes makepkg in a private owner-checked stable workspace, installs nothing, and atomically publishes exactly one package plus its SHA-256 sidecar.

The native client package smoke rejects seven hostile source fixtures, proves two builds byte-identical without changing source status, checks exact metadata, payload, modes, provenance and desktop behavior, then launches the extracted production QML root against the bounded health fixture without pacman installation.

The operator recovery drill owns two validated generated databases, migrates through the production server, applies real sysop commands, restores a custom PostgreSQL dump in isolation, compares every public application table, checks immutable report and audit state, and rejects a pre-suspension token through the restored server.
